Respondents  JUDGMENT This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act claiming for compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 30.11.2020 at about 8.00 a.m. when the petitioner was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-S- 7673 on Kunigal-Maddur Road, near JCB Kumar Haloblack Bricks factory, Beesegoweanadoddi Village, from Huliyurdurga side towards Maddur on the left side of the road

, at that time, one car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-MD-5106 driven by its driver with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner as as to endanger to human life came from behind side and dashed against the petitioner riding motor bike.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries all over the body and took treatment at hospital as inpatient.
Due to accidental injuries petitioner suffered disability and discomforts.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement.
On the other hand, inspite of service of summons respondent No.2 remained absent and hence he was placed exparte.
4. The 1st respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of the offending vehicle and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
Further this respondent has denied the age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The alleged accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the rider of the motor cycle and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
Hence, on other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.
5. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:

sentences.text:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.
 No.KA-04-MD-5106 on 30.11.2020 at  about 08.00 a.m. near Kumar Haloblack  Bricks Factory, SH-33 Road, Near
Beesegowdana Doddi H, Durga Hobli  Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and also examined another witness as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 documents.
On the other hand, respondents have not led any defence evidence.

7. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MD-5106, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex-P1 to 11 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, Mahazar in respect of vehicle, IMV report, wound certificate, Discharge summary, Charge sheet, Notarized copy of Aadhaar card, Medical bills and Medical prescriptions.
10. On the other hand, respondent No.2 owner of the offending vehicle did not appear before the court and remained absent and has been placed exparte and did not contest the matter.

Respondent No.1 Insurance company has filed the objection contending that there was a delay of 6 days in filing the complaint and further contended that the driver of offending vehicle was not possessing the driving licence to drive the car as on the date of accident and disputed that the offending vehicle has Mohammed Aleem vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123785728/
3 not been involved in the accident and due to the self fall, the petitioner has sustained the injuries.
11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the line of defence taken by the respondent No.1, on perusal of the evidence and materials on record, the accident has been taken place on 30.11.2020 at about 8.00 a.m. and admittedly the complaint has been lodged on 06.12.2020 at about 4.00 p.m., and hence there is delay of 6 days in lodging the complaint.
In Ex.P1 FIR, it is clear that as the complainant was along with petitioner in the hospital for treatment, there is a delay in filing the complaint.
Further on perusal of Ex.P6 Wound Certificate, the petitioner was taken to the hospital on 30.11.2020 at 9.00 a.m. for examination i.e., immediately soon after the accident.
Soon after the accident, the petitioner was treated in the hospital and in Ex.P6 Wound certificate, it is clearly mention that the alleged history of injury as RTA on 30.11.2020.
Thus from Ex.P6, it is clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the accident and soon after the accident, petitioner was taken the treatment in the hospital.
Even Ex.P7 Discharge summary discloses that the petitioner was admitted in the NIMANS on 01.12.2020 at about 12.24 p.m.
Thus it is clear that the petitioner has sustained the injuries due to the accident and has contended by the complainant in Ex.
P1 as he was along with the petitioner for the treatment, there may be delay of 6 days in filing the complaint.

Ordinarily prudent man would first go to the hospital for treatment soon after the accident and no prudent man would rush to the police authorities to lodge the complaint without getting the injured to hospital.

12. In this regard, I would like to rely upon the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in - (2011) 4 SCC 693 in the case of Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - " It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.

13. So, in view of the above decision, the contention taken by learned counsel for respondent no.1 that there is delay in lodging complaint etc., cannot be accepted and petitioner has satisfactorily explained the delay.
In fact, respondent has not adduced any contrary evidence to substantiate the said contention.
14. Apart from this, Ex.P3 Spot mahazar clearly shows that Kunigal-Maddur State highway-33 which runs to North to South direction.
The width of the road at 30 feet.
The accident has been taken place towards East side of the road.

Further the jurisdictional police have conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle as per Ex-P8 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, of IPC and under Sec.134(A&B), 187 of IMV Act, by holding that on 30.11.2020 at about 8.00 a.m. on Kunigal-Maddur SH-33 road, on the left of the road, when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle Honda Shine Bike bearing Reg. No.KA-42-S-7673 by Huliyurudurga towards Maddur, at the same time, accused driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-MD-5106 by name Muddasir drove his car with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner in the same direction behind the bike and hit to the back right side portion of the bike.

Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained the Mohammed Aleem vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123785728/
4 injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even Ex.P5 IMV report, it is clear that both the vehicles have been damaged and the offending vehicle has been damaged in the front portion.
Even the respondent has not given any explanation and any reasons about the reasons for damages of vehicle.
Thus Ex.P5 clearly established that the offending vehicle has been involved in the accident.
Apart from this, no material and evidence placed on record by the respondents to prove that the charge sheet is collusive and defective.

15. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
16. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
17. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988

, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

entities.text: MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
18. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-MD-5106.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
19. So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 36 years.
The petitioner has produced the Aadhar card as per Ex.P.9, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 11.10.1980 and the accident took place on 30.11.2020.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 40 years.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, he was doing Meat business and earning more than Rs.20,000/-p.m..
Due to accidental injuries, he has lost the earnings.
In support of the same, petitioner has not produced any documents.

On perusal of the wound certificate marked at Ex.P6, the petitioner has sustained Laceration over scalp, Abrasion over right arm and forearm, Abrasion over right thigh and leg and Tenderness over lower back and the doctor has opined that the said injuries are simple in nature.
20.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him to ascertain the percentage of disability suffered by him.

However, on account of the accidental injury the petitioner certainly Mohammed Aleem vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123785728/
5 undergone severe pain and mental agony.

entities.text: Mohammed Aleem vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the discharge summary Ex-P7, petitioner has taken treatment at NIMANS, Bangalore as inpatient for 4 days from 01.12.2020 to 04.12.2020.

As per Discharge summary, the petitioner has sustained the right frontal compound elevated depressed fracture post RTA and underwent left frontal craniotomy and frontal sinus exteriorisation with elevation of depressed fracture.
The petitioner has also produced medical bills at Ex.P10 for an amount of Rs.6,223/- along with Ex-P11 medical prescriptions.
The injuries suffered by petitioner necessarily caused physical discomforts with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

Moreover petitioner would obviously faced depression, disappointment & frustration and also suffered discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
21.

Hence, taking into consideration of the nature and gravity of the injuries and age and avocation of the petitioner, and the medical expenses spent by him, this tribunal deems fit to award Rs.1,00,000/- as global compensation.
Therefore, petitioner is entitle for global compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-.
22. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.
KA-04-MD-5106 and respondent No.2 being the owner thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'
24.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000=00 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, the entire amount shall be released to him through E-
payment
on proper identification and verification

. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
